[p. 444] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Surat al-Dhariyat (The Scattering Winds)**

Its central aim (*maqsud*) is to demonstrate the truth of what Surat Qaf warned of explicitly and gave glad tidings of allusively, especially its final part concerning the calamities of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. Its name, *al-Dhariyat*, points clearly to this when one considers the response to the oath, for with the oath, because of the strength of the connection, it is like a single verse, even though the oath consists of five elements. The expression for the winds as *al-dhariyat* is the most complete indication of this. Their denial of the threat is because they perceive none of its causes, although those causes are present among them, just as the causes of what comes from the clouds, of mercy and of vengeance, are present even though they are not seen, namely the winds, even though they do not see them. The nature of the wind is to *dharw* (scatter), which is dispersal. When Allah wills, the winds gather, and what He wills comes to pass. They scatter the vapours, and when Allah, glorified is He, wills to gather them, He causes them to be carried by what He has placed within them, loading them with it, and He sets them in motion with ease. From them He apportions, as He wills, at times lightning and at other times thunder, which resounds like the clash of iron upon iron, or of stone upon its like, together with the subtlety of the clouds, with all that is observed in them of causes. At other times it is heavy rain pouring down, sometimes hail, sometimes snow, which is both hoped for and feared, and at certain moments thunderbolts and fires of a fierce burning, and at other moments jewels and coral of wondrous beauty. Thus it is at one time (p. 445) joy and good pleasure, and at another grief and sorrow, loss and ruin. Moreover, they are the most skilled of people in some of these matters, knowing the cloud that promises rain and the one that does not, the one whose rain is near, and the one that has not yet been ready to rain. And there are many other things that the people of literature have recorded and that the people of language have transmitted from them. All of this is by the directing of the angels under the command of Allah. For this reason, and Allah knows best, it was prescribed (*sunna*) to say upon hearing thunder: "Glory be to Allah, the Holy, the Most Holy," to make clear that the true director is Allah, exalted is He, "Lord of the angels" (i.e., those appointed for this task), "and of the Spirit" (i.e., that which this body carries of rain, fire, or other things). And Allah is the Granter of success.

"In the name of Allah," who encompasses all attributes of perfection, so He does not break His promise. "The Most Gracious," who has encompassed creation with the blessing of bringing into being. "The Most Merciful," who has specially favoured whoever He has chosen with success in what He is pleased with of the purposes.

* *

When He, glorified is He, concluded Surat Qaf with the reminder of the threat, He opened this surah with an oath emphatic in confirming its truth. He said, linking the oath with what it swears to: ﴿By the scattering winds﴾, i.e., the winds whose nature is to lift, to scatter, to disperse and to carry away. He confirmed this with His words: ﴿scattering them far and wide﴾, i.e., by what the angels direct them to. Al-Isfahani said: The winds are beneath the wings of the Cherubim, the bearers of the Throne. From there they stir, and they fall upon the orbit of the sun. Then they stir away from the orbit of the sun and fall upon the mountaintops, and from the mountaintops they fall upon the land. As for the north wind, it passes beneath Eden and takes from the fragrance of its perfume, and passes over the spirits of the righteous. Then it takes its boundary from the Chair of the Bear (Banat Na'sh) to the west of the sun. The west wind comes with its boundary from the west of the sun to the rising of Suhayl (Canopus). The south wind comes with its boundary from the rising of Suhayl to the rising of the sun. The east wind comes with its boundary from the rising of the sun to the Chair of the Bear, so that none of these enters the boundary of the others [nor the other into the boundary of this one].

Since the goal of scattering is to prepare for carrying, He said, linking by consequence and sequence: ﴿Then those that carry﴾, i.e., of the clouds, which the wind has scattered from their origin, which is the vapors, and which it has lifted up into the air in the direction of height, then gathered together, so that it became a cloud, and then spread it out along with its coming together. Then Allah loaded it with what He placed in it of His will: water, thunderbolts, and other things.

﴿A heavy load﴾, i.e., a weighty burden. Before that, none of it or what it carries was seen, so know the power of Allah over everything He wills, even if you do not see its causes. ﴿And let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah.﴾

Since the carrying (al-ḥaml) is in fact the placing [of the rain] in the places where harm or benefit is intended, and since the movement of the clouds after carrying [the water], across the expanse of the air and the open horizon, without any visible holder, is a greater proof of power, especially when it comes with the swift running for which proverbs are coined for speed, and likewise the running of ships across the open sea after their heaviness with cargo (p-447), He said: ﴿And those that glide with ease﴾, i.e., gliding with facility.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 4:

When it was at the utmost degree of indication of complete power, through the drowning of what is carried in lands that are swept away, especially if the places where it is poured out and the spots where it is spilled are far apart, and that dispersal [being] the utmost of the flowing that follows from the carrying that follows from the scattering, He said, causing it to follow and be consequent, pointing by the form of intensive verb (al-taf'il) to the strangeness of its separating its drops and the wondrousness of its dispersing them, so as to spare them from its punishment, and other than that from the conditions of the things that flow and the turning of the things that run: ﴿Then those that distribute (al-muqassimat)﴾, i.e., from the clouds, by what the angels, peace be upon them, turn them in; and likewise the ships, by what God turns them by of gentle or stormy winds, of safety and ruin, of speed and slowness; and likewise others of these, of every matter that the angels turn and divide among the servants.

Since what is carried is varied, as has preceded, He said, gathering all of that: ﴿Affairs (amran)﴾, i.e., of mercy or of punishment. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': These are oaths that God swears by and that creatures do not swear by, because the oath of creatures is a seeking of testimony for the soundness of their saying by one who knows the secret as the open, and that is God Most High; whereas the oath of the Creator is the intention of affirming the report in their souls, so He swears by some of the wonders of His creation in a manner that necessitates reflection and points to His oneness. So the winds, by their blowing and their stillness, for the gathering of clouds and the scattering of seeds, and the variation of the air, their being strong at one time and gentle at another; and the clouds, by their standing, heavy with water, without pillars, and by their being turned away at the time of need for them by that which, were it to persist, would destroy, and were it to cease, no one would be able to get a drop from them; and by the dispersal of the rain, for otherwise the tillage and the offspring would perish; and the ships, by the subjection of the sea for their running and the ordaining of the wind for them, by what, were it to increase, would drown them, and were it to become still, would destroy them; and the angels who divide the affairs by the command of their Lord. All of this is evidence of the existence of the Wise Maker, the Originator, the All-Knowing, the Powerful, the Glorious, the Generous.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 5:

Since they were denying the threat, He emphasized the answer after emphasis by the very oath itself, saying: ﴿Indeed what﴾ [i.e., that which] ﴿you are promised﴾, i.e., of the promise to the obedient and the threat to the disobedient, even though you do not see its causes. And since what they were threatened with is so certain in its occurrence and so near, it is as if it were present, addressing them of its own self, He expressed the verbal noun (al-masdar) by the active participle, saying: ﴿is surely true﴾, i.e., its report is in exact conformity with reality. You will see its conformity when it occurs, and you will know that this reality is a firm truth, not an imagination, due to its conformity with the report.

Ibn Burjan said: Know that God, Mighty and Majestic, did not swear by any oath except that its meaning corresponds to meanings in the thing sworn about, by a shining lamp through which God guides whom He wills. What blinds one from seeing that are the outward forms of sensible things, and what deafens one from hearing their call is the clamor of what is witnessed; were it not so, they would be called to it from a near place.

Al-Bayda'awi said: It is as if He cited His power over these wondrous things, which contravene the requirement of nature, as evidence of His power over resurrection.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 6:

When the time of their threat and what pertains to the recompense on the Day of Resurrection had come, and they were denying it, He said: ﴿Indeed, the Recompense is surely to come﴾, meaning the requital of every person for what they earned on the Day of Resurrection, and the sharʿ (religious law) with which I sent this noble Prophet. It is inevitable, even if you deny it. So his religion will prevail over all religions, as He promised, and then We will bring all people together for the reckoning. (p-449)

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said in his Burhan: When He, glory be to Him, mentioned the promises of the Hereafter in the surah "Qaf" and the magnitude of those states, from His saying: ﴿And the stupor of death will come with truth﴾ [Qaf: 19] to the end of the surah, He followed that with an oath to affirm its occurrence and truthfulness, and said: ﴿By the winds that scatter dust﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 1], [up] to His saying: ﴿What you are promised is surely true﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 5]. ﴿And indeed, the Recompense is surely to come.﴾ The din (recompense) is the requital, meaning that they will be repaid for what they did and will be given their full share of their deeds. ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do﴾ [Ibrahim: 42]. ﴿We only give them respite so that they may increase in sin﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178]. When Allah swore to the truth of His promise and the occurrence of recompense, He followed that with their denial of recompense and their scorn, and said: ﴿They ask, "When is the Day of Recompense?"﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 12]. Then He, exalted is He, mentioned the state of the two groups and the end of the two paths, up to His saying: ﴿And on the earth are signs for those who are certain﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 20]. He rebuked whoever does not exercise their thought or extend their gaze to what He, glory be to Him, deposited in the world of wonders. He then followed this with references to the conditions of past nations and what their denial led to. All of this is a call to extend the gaze to His saying: ﴿And of everything We created pairs﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 49], with His saying: ﴿Thus did no messenger come to those before them but they said, "A sorcerer or a madman!"﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 52], meaning: this is their habit and custom, as if they had made a covenant on it and passed it on to one another. Then He said, exalted is He: (p-450) ﴿Did they bequeath it to one another? Rather, they are a transgressing people﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 53], meaning: how strange it is that they proceed in denial and corruption in one single course. Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿Rather, they are a transgressing people﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 53], meaning that the cause of their denial is the one that is unified, so its effect is unified too, and the cause is their transgression and the darkening of their hearts by what preceded. ﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾ [al-Sajdah: 13]. Then He added for His Prophet, peace be upon him, matters that came in the manner of giving him the choice regarding them, from His saying: ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not to be blamed﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 54]. Then He indicated, by His saying: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 55], that securing his reward, peace be upon him, lies only in reminding and calling to Allah, exalted is He, and then Allah benefits by that whoever has been preordained to happiness. ﴿Only those who hear will respond﴾ [al-An'am: 36]. Then He informed His Prophet, prayers and peace be upon him, that their denial of him will bring them a share and portion of what overtook others who committed the same acts as them and took the same path as them. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, for those who did wrong is a portion like the portion of their companions﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 59], to the end of the surah. End quote.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 7:

When He, glory be to Him, had informed of the steadfastness of His report, He followed it with the informing of the feebleness of their speech. So He said, swearing an oath upon it, for the exaggeration of their emphasis on its meanings while being contradictory in His beautiful action and His magnificent craftsmanship, indicating that they had not taken on the character of His good qualities, neither by speech nor by deed: ﴿By the sky, full of paths﴾, that is: the signs interlaced with the paths of the stars (p-451), which are firm, good in their craftsmanship, excellent in their arrangement and adornment, to the point that they seem woven, beautiful in their craft, magnificent in their effects, combining cutting and intermingling, agreement and difference. The root of ḥabk is ihkām (firm making) in extension and continuity; so said al-Razi in al-Lawami'.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 8:

﴿Indeed you﴾ O assembly of Quraysh, ﴿are in a word﴾ encompassing you regarding the matter of the Qur'an and the one who brought it, and all the matter of your religion and other than it, of what you intend thereby to nullify the true religion, ﴿that is contradictory﴾ like the contradiction of the paths of the sky, which hardly are arranged in order, and whose first cannot be known from its last. And the contradiction of these things sworn by at the beginning of the surah, and the contradiction of their purposes. But despite that, it is mutually conflicting. And even if you strive to adorn it, bring it close to understanding, and beautify it, when a critic presents it to penetrating thought, it hardly is governed by any governing principle, nor is it bound by any binding. Rather, at one time you say: "This is poetry," and then it would be necessary for you to describe it with what you describe poetry by, namely consistency in pure meter and a unified rhyme, and sweetness and elegance. At another time you say: "This is sorcery," and then it would be necessary for you, along with acknowledging incapacity regarding it, that it has no realities [of its own]. In fact, no person of understanding contemplates it without seeing its realities to be more firmly established than the mountains. At another time you say: "A confusion of dreams," and then it would be necessary for you that it is not governed by any governing principle, and that it has no meaning that can be grasped, and that no one is unable to fabricate its like. Thus you have nullified your saying that it is poetry and that it is sorcery.

At another time you say: "It is soothsaying," and then it would be necessary for you to believe of it what you believe of the sayings of soothsayers, of reporting unseen matters, disclosing what is hidden, and deciding judgments. So you have nullified what preceded of your statements: "a confusion of dreams," "sorcery," and "poetry." At another time you say: "It is madness," and thus you have undone all your previous statements and called out against yourselves with confounding. You say of the one who brought it that he is a poet, a sorcerer, a madman, a soothsayer, and a liar, and each of these statements contradicts the others. Yet you claim that you are the most truthful of people, the furthest from the shame of lying, and that you are the most intelligent of people and the most just. Thus, first, your statements have differed from one another, and then they have differed from your actions. So the contradiction of the paths of the stars indicates a preventer who chooses, of perfect knowledge and complete power, and likewise the contradiction of your saying in this manner, together with the intellects you possess, indicates a dominator over you in that regard. Thus these are two signs, in the horizons and in your own selves.

Since this disagreement is something that can hardly be believed, for no sensible person would fall into it, he explained its cause: that they are overpowered by the force of the hand of power. So he said: ﴿Is turned away﴾, meaning: he is diverted, by the most trivial and easiest matter, from the ways of uprightness, and turned from his face to his back. ﴿From it﴾, meaning: his turning away from this saying proceeds figuratively from what its shame entails for him; so for this reason he says it. ﴿Whoever is turned away﴾, meaning: he has been turned by a overpowering turning. That is, through this turning, which is the greatest of turnings, it becomes clear that He issued a judgment from eternity, a firm and comprehensive judgment, so that no saying or deed turns one away from it except that his face is turned to his back (p-453), and he cannot bring forth from himself anything upon his face. Thus it is as if there is no one turned away like him, because of the intensity of his aversion and the strangeness of his condition.

Since lying is reporting what has no reality and deliberately fabricating, and since al-kharṣ (conjecture) comprises lying, fabrication, contradiction, and every saying based on mere supposition, He said, making known what is due to them for their saying this: "They were killed, or you were killed" — this was the original form, but He made apparent the description they deserved by their saying: ﴿Cursed be the conjecturers﴾. That is, the killing of liars occurred by the easiest matter, and inevitably of every killer, and of those who speak by conjecture, who cut their speech from a root that is not fit for conjecture, which is severance. They are those who speak without support from a Book, a Sunnah, or a remnant of knowledge (athāra min ʿilm). And it is a supplication (duʿāʾ) or a report, because it is answered.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 11:

﴿Those who are﴾ specifically ﴿in a flood﴾, that is, in depths of blindness and misguidance, drowning in their intoxication and ignorance which has submerged them. For this reason they are agitated like one who walks in the middle of the sea, so that no matter of speech, action or state is ever set in order for him. ﴿Heedless﴾, that is, deeply immersed in heedlessness (sahw), which is forgetfulness, unawareness, bewilderment, and the heart's departure toward something other than what concerns it. Thus the one who does this is of varied conditions, owing to the terror of what he is in and the severity of his distress.

When he had judged their heedlessness, he pointed to it with his saying: ﴿They ask﴾, meaning: time after time, continuously, mocking their own words: ﴿When is﴾, meaning: when will it be, and at what time, ﴿the Day of Judgment﴾, meaning: the occurrence of the recompense which he informs us of. Had they not been in this state (p-454), they would have reflected within themselves that none of them sends out his slaves or his hired workers to any task without calling them to account for their deeds, certainly observing their conditions and judging between them regarding their words and actions. How then could it be supposed of the Most Wise of judges that He would leave His servants, whom He created upon this firmly ordered system, and originated for them these two horizons, and prepared for their sake within them what they need, for provision for the Return, leaving them neglected (sudan), bringing them into existence in vain (ʿabathan)?

As the matter of the Resurrection had been established by the expression "those who are heedless" (bi-sahun), He said: ﴿On the Day﴾, that is, We will say on the Day ﴿when they will be tried over the Fire﴾, that is, they will be thrown into it and burned, and tormented, and they will be... [of] the disputing, being told, by way of rebuke and reproach:

**Qur'an 51:14:** ﴿Taste your trial⦆ ... the punishment, from the encompassing trial, and your hastening of what you were promised, mocking and denying. ﴿This is what you used to seek to hasten.﴾ That is: you were asking for its speedy arrival.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 15:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing﴾, that is: those for whom taqwa (God-consciousness) was a constant attribute, ﴿will be in gardens﴾, that is: great orchards, into which We enter ...

﴿and springs﴾

﴿Receiving what﴾, that is, everything, ﴿their Lord has given them﴾, that is, the One who does good to them, ... with the completeness of His knowledge and the all-encompassing scope of His power. He leaves them no pleasure without bestowing it upon them, so they accept it with the utmost eagerness, because it is of the greatest preciousness. Since this is a great matter, about whose cause the mind wanders in every direction, he gave its reason by saying, emphasizing the attribution to the disbelievers of wrongdoing: ﴿Indeed they were﴾, that is, in a state that was like an innate disposition. Since a person is either obedient throughout his whole life or in part of it... to obedience, and obedience erases what came before it and becomes a cause for changing evil deeds into good deeds, as a bounty from Him, glorified is He, each of the two categories was obedient throughout his entire time. He removed the preposition (jār) and said: ﴿before that﴾, that is, in the abode of action. It was also said: they received what was prescribed for them with the utmost acceptance, because before the prescription of the obligations they used to act out of love. This is the meaning of ﴿doers of good﴾, that is, in their dealings with the Creator and with creation, worshipping God as if they saw Him. Then he explained their good deeds, expressing them by what is in the utmost exaggeration, with his saying:

﴿كانُوا﴾ means: because of the honour and love they had for Him, it was as if they were disposed to it by nature. For the sake of emphasis, the predication is attributed to them twice. ﴿قَلِيلا مِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ refers to the night, which is the time of rest and the fulfilment of desires. He reinforces the meaning by affirming ”ما“ (ma, the negative particle), so He says: ﴿ما يَهْجَعُونَ﴾, meaning they do hujū' (hujū', light, brief sleep). So consider what lies beyond that. The sentence affirms their hujū', which is sleep taken for rest and to relieve fatigue, and it negates it. He mentions the night to confirm the meaning, since hujū' is sleep at night. The meaning is that they spend most of the night in worship and sleep only a small part of it.

The one who does good, since he never sees himself as anything but falling short, said, indicating this and also that their night prayer is joined to the last part of the night, emphasizing it by the attribution (al-isnad) twice more as well: ﴿And at the dawns﴾. Ibn Zayd said: al-saḥar (the last part of the night) is the final sixth of the night.

﴿They﴾, that is, constantly, both outwardly and inwardly, ﴿seek forgiveness﴾, that is, despite this striving they count themselves as sinners and ask for the forgiveness of their sins, because of the abundance of their knowledge of God, and that they are unable to appraise Him as He truly deserves, however hard they strive, in accordance with the saying of the master of creation: "I cannot count the praises upon You." The explicit mention of the pronoun (ibrāz al-ḍamīr) indicates (p-456) that if anyone else had done this for a single night, he would have been pleased with himself and thought that no one was better than him. It also indicates that their seeking forgiveness so often requires that they be in a state where it is presumed that they are more deserving of humility than those who persist in sins. Their seeking forgiveness is with insight, because they reflected on what belongs to Him, glorified is He, in the horizons and in themselves of signs and far-reaching wisdoms that cannot be counted, so they knew that He is worthy of being obeyed and feared. They strove and abandoned sleep, and let their tears flow. Then they set this against His favors, and behold, their works were in the utmost shortfall, so they turned to seeking forgiveness, knowing that He cannot be appraised as He truly deserves.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 19:

When he mentioned their dealing with the Creator (al-Khaliq), he followed it with their dealing with creation (al-khala'iq), completing the reality of ihsan (excellence in conduct), so he said: ﴿And in their wealth there was a right﴾, i.e., of all its kinds, ﴿for the beggar and the deprived﴾, i.e., a fixed portion. Since the context here is that of ihsan, their ihsan was due to their intense love for the servants of Allah, which does not hold them back from what is obligatory, unlike what is in "sa'ala" (the context of those who pray in general), where he left out describing it as known (al-ma'lumiyya), so he said: ﴿for the beggar﴾, i.e., the one who makes his need known by asking people, and he is the mutakaffif (the one who asks persistently). ﴿And the deprived﴾, and he is the mutaʿaffif (the one who restrains himself from asking), who does not find what suffices him, and does not ask people, and is not noticed so that charity might be given to him. This is the description of the People of the Suffa (Ahl al-Suffa), may Allah be pleased with them. So the good-doers recognize the person with this description by their penetrating insight, and Allah's care for them (is what enables this).

When his oath by the sky and by what precedes it, the scattering winds (al-Dhariyat), pointed to the signs in the heavenly realm, and he concluded with the wealth that the earth produces, the sense became: "In the heavens are signs for the believers," showing His greatness and His deserving of worship in utmost submission, with desire and fear. He then joined to it His words: ﴿And in the earth﴾, which likewise contains the diversity of many different minerals, all of one origin, along with plants, animals, inanimate things, land and sea, and other secrets that point to the Chooser who acts by choice. ﴿Are signs﴾, meaning great indications which, though clear upon reflection, are also subtle. ﴿For those with certainty﴾, those for whom certainty has become a firm, innate disposition. Because of this, they perceive what is in them, along with the causes connected to them, yet those causes do not occupy them, and they do not stop at most of the causes of the signs within them. This leads them to certainty about what the messengers have warned of, such as resurrection and other matters that reason can establish on its own.

Al-Qushayri said: Among the signs in the earth is that it carries everything. Likewise, the knower (al-'arif) bears with everyone. Whoever finds someone burdensome or is annoyed by seeing someone does so because he is absent from the Reality and beholds creation through the eye of division. The people of the realities do not possess this trait. Among the signs in the earth is that all filth and refuse are thrown upon it, yet it makes every flower and blossom grow. Likewise, the knower absorbs the harshness he encounters and gives forth only every noble character and pure disposition.

When he had pointed to the signs of the horizons, he followed them with the signs within the souls, saying: ﴿And in yourselves﴾, meaning: among the signs that you share with inanimate matter (*jamad*), and then you separated from it by growth (*numuww*), then by sense perception (*hiss*), then you surpassed the lowly animal by intellect (*'aql*), which leads to the wonders of knowledge and the subtleties of understanding. (p-458) Since these are the most manifest of the signs, his drawing attention to them gave rise to a rebuke for their failure to take heed of them, so he said: ﴿Will you not then see?﴾, meaning: with your eyes and your insight, so that you may contemplate what these signs contain and reflect on whether you see the causes of most of them. For all of these are signs indicating the power of the Maker (*al-Sani'*) over everything He wills and His choice, and that He did not create this creation in vain, so He must gather them to Him for the reckoning before Him. The certain believers never cease to look at such things with seeing eyes and penetrating understandings, so whenever they see a sign, they take a lesson from it, and their faith increases upon their faith, and their certainty upon their certainty. The first thing they perceive from the signs deposited in them is need, so whoever contemplates them knows that he is a servant, and whenever he knows this, he knows that he has a Lord who is not in need. Whoever sees all the attributes and names, and whose understanding penetrates into the subtleties of created beings, rises to the highest ranks.

When al-Biqa'i had shown, through what I put forward in ﴿By those who distribute affairs﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 4], what lies in the direction of height of the causes that bring about blessing and punishment, he said: ﴿And in the heaven﴾, meaning the direction of height, ﴿is your provision﴾, through what comes of rain, winds, heat, cold and other things that He, glory be to Him, has ordained for the benefit of His servants, ﴿and what you are promised﴾. All that the Messengers brought you of promise and threat, of the thunderclap and the earthquake and other terrors and causes of retribution, and likewise mercy, good and blessing, and everything that hopes attach themselves to. Just as you believe in these while you do not see them, so believe in Paradise and Hell even though you have not seen them. For there is no difference between water that Allah sends down, from which there come gardens and orchards, and thorns, ailments (p-459) [and] bitternesses, poisons, scorpions and serpents, reptiles, beasts of prey and creeping things; and water with which He brings the dead back to life, then gathers them to gardens and fires. Just as there is no doubt about the manifestation of this unseen matter, [so there is no confusion about the manifestation of that unseen matter].

Also among the meanings: you should not preoccupy yourself with provision, for it is in the heaven, and you have no way to ascend to it. Occupy yourself instead with the service you have been charged with, for the One who holds the provision. Provision is in the heaven, and to it the deed is raised. If you want your provision to descend to you, then send up to it the righteous part of your deeds. For this reason they said: prayer is the branch of the door of provision. ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you﴾ [Taha: 132].

When he swore by what is within His power for those who stop at the perceptible and well-known things, so that they rise thereby to the highest ranks, and His perfection became fully manifest, and they knew that in His treasuries (khaza'in) is everything the Messengers told of concerning promise and threat, He made the following statement as a consequence, swearing by His most holy Self but in a familiar manner, saying: ﴿So by the Lord of the heaven and the earth﴾, i.e., the Originator and Manager (of the heaven and the earth), with what He deposited in them of what you know and what you do not know. ﴿Indeed it﴾, i.e., what you are promised of good and evil, of Paradise and Hellfire, and the oath preceding it confirms that it is true, ﴿is truth﴾, i.e., established, to which reality conforms. Thus He combined truth (haqq) with truthfulness (sidq). ﴿Just as it is that you﴾, i.e., while you are equal to the rest of what is on the earth of inanimate things and others, ﴿speak﴾, a speech renewed at every moment and continuous, which is not imagination or magic. That is: (p-٤٦٠) that is true just as it is true that this is true. He who gave you the power of speech from among what is on the earth, through causes you do not see and cannot count, and along with that, He gave the rest of them causes [like that], is capable of bringing about His promise of provision and other things, as long as you need that, by what He placed in you of life, through which knowledge is sound, and from that knowledge arises speech, which makes you need provision from whatever direction they seek, even if you do not see its causes. Just as, if He willed, He would make all who are in the heavens and the earth, of inanimate things, speak, by establishing for them causes like those He established for you, even if you do not see that.

When he had explained, through what preceded of the oath and what followed it, that He had placed in the heavens and the earth, and between them, means suited to bringing about what We had promised of good and what We had threatened of evil, even though we have not seen them, and He is capable and free to choose, that became as though it were witnessed, and there is no ground for denying either promise or threat. He pointed to this and depicted it through what had been witnessed of the states of past peoples. And He began, because the context concerns the good-doers (al-muhsinun), with the chief of the good-doers among the people of these reports, the one whom the angels, peace be upon them, informed of what would come about through him, even though it was contrary to the usual course. So his wife was astonished at this, although she was the most eminent of the women of her time. He followed his story with the story of Lot, his brother's son, peace be upon them both, because the two stories are connected in time, and because their punishment corresponds to what He swore by at the beginning of the surah. For He, glory be to Him, commanded the scattering winds (al-Dhariyat), and they uprooted them from their towns, lifted them up as clouds are lifted, then overturned them and pelted them with stones, and commanded the earth, and it swallowed them up, and the angels charged with such things. (p. 461) They carried out everything they had been commanded, and they saw them in their town and aimed at them with a plot, because their affair was hidden from them. And they came to the Friend (al-Khalil), peace be upon him, who was the most eminent of his time, while they were in that state, and at first he knew nothing of their condition and did not take them to be anything but human beings. So he said, magnifying the matter of the story by addressing the most eminent of creation and the most perceptive of them in understanding, indicating that no one else understands this as it should be understood, in the form of a question, according to the custom of the Arabs in informing about past events, even though the one informing knows that the one addressed has no knowledge of it, because the purpose is only to draw attention to the fact that this matter deserves concern and investigation so that its great matters may be known. Abu Hayyan said: It is a preparatory statement (taqrir) so that the listener's soul may gather, as when you want to tell someone of something wondrous and first ask him: Have you heard of such a thing or not? As though you were prompting him to say: No, and to ask you for the account [al-hadith]. End of quote.

﴿Has there reached you﴾, O most perfect of creation, ﴿the story of the honored guests﴾, he referred to them in the singular to indicate the unity of their word, ﴿of Abraham﴾, who is Our friend, and it shows that he did not recognize anything of what they had brought, which indicates that they were a group. ﴿The honored﴾, that is, those who possess honor, and Abraham, peace be upon him, was the most honored of them through his word and his deed. So in his account there is a clear sign, according to what has been shown in this surah, of God's power and the truth of His promise and His threat, together with the consolation it contains for you and for those who follow you, and good tidings of the honoring of the one who affirms and the humiliation of the one who denies. Al-Qushayri said: It was said that their number was twelve angels; it was said that it was Gabriel, peace be upon him, and nine were with him; (p. 462) and it was said: they were three:

﴿إذْ﴾ (idh), meaning "when": that is, the account of them is (when) ﴿they entered upon him﴾, that is, entering with an air of dignity (istiʿlāʾ), unlike the entry of the rest of the guests. ﴿Then they said, "Peace."﴾ That is, they spoke. Then he resumed reporting his reply with his words: ﴿He said, "Peace."﴾ That is, he said it with his tongue: ﴿Peace﴾ means established and lasting, so it is better than their greeting.

Since what has been mentioned of their entry and their greeting was not strange to those addressed by this account, and since the story had begun with what indicates the strangeness of what is being related from it, the listener's interest was aroused toward what came after this. He was answered with his words: ﴿"A people unknown."﴾ That is, they are people of strength for what they undertake and stand firm in, and ﴿unknown﴾ (munkarūn) means their state is such that it is fit to be disliked by one who disapproves. He placed this (the word ﴿unknown﴾) ahead of its proper position, which seemed more fitting at first glance, and for clarification, because the context (of the story) concerns the hiddenness of causes from a human being and their remoteness, even though they are at the utmost clarity and nearness, even if he is at the utmost height. Indeed, his disapproval of them came after the bringing of the food, because they had not eaten. This statement was within himself and he did not confront them with it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 26:

When he indicated that, upon denying them, he did not recognize what kind they were nor the specifics of their situation, he arranged upon his returning their greeting that he hastened with extreme speed to bring what is fitting for a guest, assuming they were humans. So he said: ﴿Then he turned away﴾ (p-463), meaning: he went off secretly, swiftly, and to places of concealment away from their eyes, as is part of the etiquette of hospitality, fearing that they would forbid him or that waiting would trouble them: ﴿to his family﴾ [i.e.] those who had a cow with them, ﴿and brought a fatted calf﴾, meaning: a young one from the offspring of cattle, ﴿fat﴾, having already roasted it and cooked it thoroughly.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 27:

﴿So he brought it near to them﴾. Since he had informed them of what was appropriate to mention concerning the matter of hospitality, namely the eating, it is known that the implied sense is: it was as if it were said, "What did he say to them when they did not eat?" It is said: ﴿He said﴾ [i.e., being exceedingly courteous, hinting at disapproval]: ﴿Will you not eat?﴾ i.e., of it.

So when it was as if it had been said, "Then they did not eat," he (the Qur'an) made the following statement its consequence: ﴿So he sensed fear within himself﴾, that is, he concealed it deep within his inmost self as an inner state, ﴿of them﴾, because of their refusing to eat; for when he saw their turning away from the food, his thoughts took every direction regarding the reason for their coming to him. ﴿They said﴾, comforting him: ﴿Do not fear﴾, and they informed him that they were ﴿messengers of Allah﴾. ﴿And they gave him the glad tidings of a boy﴾, despite his old age and his wife's despair, since she was advanced in years after having been barren; he was Isaac, peace be upon him. And since the context concerns the hiddenness of the causes, it was at the peak of eloquence that He described him with the words ﴿knowing﴾, that is, one created with a nature prepared for knowledge, who will not die until his knowledge becomes manifest in action at its appointed time.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 29:

When the two were far from being receptive to a child, the following statement was made as a consequence of that, indicating that the child is Isaac (Is'haq), together with the indication that the concealment of causes does not affect the existence of the things caused: ﴿Then his wife came forward﴾, that is, upon hearing these words, ﴿his wife﴾. Since she had become filled with wonder, he expressed it with the vessel (of the circumstance), saying: ﴿in a loud cry﴾, that is, a cry and a commotion of shrieking that had enveloped her, so their thoughts went in every direction about it. ﴿Then she struck﴾, that is, she slapped, out of her astonishment, with the tips of her fingers, the act of one amazed, ﴿her face﴾, in order to dispel the causes of a child in her knowledge, owing to habit, while knowing that the effective factor lies in the Causer and not in the causes, even if the causes are sound. Al-Baghawi said: The root of the word "sakk" is striking one thing against a broad thing. ﴿And she said﴾, wishing to clarify the matter, whether the child is from her or from another: ﴿an old woman﴾, and with old age ﴿barren﴾. So in the time of her youth she did not accept conception. Al-Qushayri, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It was said that she was, on that day, a daughter of ninety-eight years.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 30:

When this was the case, [in what was said], her longing for the answer was at its greatest, so God, exalted is He, resumed the answer with His words: ﴿They said: "Thus"﴾, that is: like what we have said of this great glad tidings, ﴿said your Lord﴾, that is: the One who does good to you by qualifying you for this, in accordance with what you mentioned of your condition, and by qualifying you before, through being joined to His Friend (ﷺ). Since the focus of her wonder was that this happened in the days of her youth, [the angels] gave the reason for their announcement as a confirmation of it, emphasizing it because her words and her action were the action of one who denies, even though she intended by them only to seek assurance: ﴿Indeed, He is﴾, that is: He alone, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, who places things in their most fitting places (p-465). Thus He ordered the greatness of this newborn upon both your barrenness and your incapacity. Then they gave the reason for that by their words: ﴿the All-Wise﴾, that is: the One whose knowledge encompasses all, so He is such that nothing can incapacitate Him, for what preceded of the proof in Surah "Ta-Ha" that the comprehensiveness of knowledge necessarily entails the all-encompassing scope of power.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 31:

Since al-Khalil (ʿalayhi al-salam, the Friend of God, Abraham) was the most knowledgeable of the people of his time in divine matters, he knew that the gathering of the angels in that form in which he saw them was not for this glad tidings alone. Therefore God, exalted is He, resumed the answer for one who would seem to be asking: "What was his state and their state after this?" by His saying: ﴿He said﴾, meaning: he said, as a consequence of what he saw of their condition: ﴿"What is your business?"﴾, meaning: what is your great news, ﴿O messengers?﴾, meaning: for a great matter.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 32:

﴿Qālū﴾ (They said), asserting with emphasis that the content of their report is a decree that cannot be avoided, and that intercession has no place in it: ﴿Innā ursilnā﴾ (Indeed, we have been sent), i.e., by the sending of One whom you know, ﴿ilā qawmin mujrimīn﴾ (to a people who are criminals), i.e., they are at the utmost degree of strength in what they attempt, and they have diverted the strength with which Allah favoured them toward severing what ought to be joined and joining what ought to be severed.
"To send down upon them" — that is, from the heaven in which is what the servants were promised and threatened with — "stones of clay" — that is, prepared for burning and for setting alight.

"Musawwamah" (﴿مُسَوَّمَةً﴾): that is, marked with a sign of the specific punishment.

Since they had seen his concern to know about their affair, fearing that they might have been sent to punish someone whose matter weighed heavily upon him, they set his fear at ease by describing his kindness, saying: ﴿Near your Lord﴾, that is, the One who shows kindness to you by this good news and other things, ﴿for the transgressors﴾ [that is] those who exceed the limits, not content with what has been permitted to them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 35:

Since it is known that the people are sometimes in a town (madar) and sometimes in a village (sha'r), and it is known from the preceding verses that the punishment is specific to those given to excess (al-israf), he derived from that, detailing their report, the statement of the Exalted, informing that they were in a town (madar): ﴿So We brought out﴾ by the greatness We possess, after Our messengers had gone to them and there had occurred between them and Lut, peace be upon him, well-known attempts which the situation here does not call for mentioning. The angels were the cause of their punishment, and the people of the town who were attempting in their affair did not know this. And this expression, if it is a report to us, is a report of what occurred so that we may take heed from it; and if it was addressed to Ibrahim, peace be upon him, its meaning is that the greatest judgment occurred by their removal, as good news to him of their deliverance. ﴿of those who were in it﴾, that is, its villages. And since the heart is the pillar of the body, upon which its soundness or corruption depends, and its action is the best of actions, for by it occurs the submission of the limbs or their recalcitrance, he began with it, saying: ﴿of the believers﴾, that is, those who affirm with their hearts, because We do not equate them with the criminals; so We delivered them from the punishment despite their paucity and weakness and the strength and multitude of the opponents. And he derived from the frowning, the concealment, and the attention to outward and inward matters, his statement:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 36:

﴿Fa-mā wajadnā﴾ He attributed the act to Himself, honouring His messengers and informing that their action is His action. ﴿fīhā ghayra bayt﴾ (not) a single house, which was the house of Lūṭ, son of the brother of Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him). It was said: the number of those saved from them was thirteen. Since al-islām (submission, lit. "Islam") may be applied to the outward only, even though the intended meaning here is the more specific, He placed it later and said: ﴿min al-muslimīn﴾ (of those who submit), i.e., those firmly rooted in submission (islām), outwardly and inwardly, to Allah without any objection at all, and they are Ibrāhīm and his family (peace be upon them). For they were the first in whom complete submission was found, and they were named by it, as has passed in al-Baqarah, and they named their followers by it. So this single house was one to which both faith (īmān), which is affirmation (taṣdīq), and submission (islām), which is surrender (inqiyād), truly apply. Al-Baghawī said: Allah the Exalted described them with both faith and submission together, because no believer believes except that he is a submitter. He means that there is a necessary connection between them, even though the two concepts differ. Al-Aṣbahānī said: [And] it was said: Lūṭ and the people of his house who were saved were thirteen.

And when the survival of the traces of those who were destroyed was a stronger proof of the power of the One who destroyed them, He said: ﴿And We left﴾, meaning, by the greatness We possess, ﴿in it﴾, meaning in those towns, by the punishment We inflicted on them. Its beginning was most fitting to the act of the scattering winds (al-Dhariyat) that carry clouds, for We uprooted all their towns and they rose into the air like clouds, up to the heights of the sky, and none of their people perceived anything of that. Then they were overturned, stones were made to follow them, and they were swallowed by the earth. They were submerged in water that resembles none of the waters of the earth, just as their wickedness did not resemble the wickedness of anyone among the people of the earth who came before them. ﴿A sign﴾, meaning a great indication of Our power over whatever We will, ﴿for those who fear﴾, as was mentioned at the end of Surah Qaf, that they are the ones truly addressed by the warning, because they are the ones who benefit from it, rather than the one whose heart has hardened and who does not take heed. ﴿the painful punishment﴾, meaning that it should descend upon them as it descended upon these towns in this world: the angels lifting them into the scattering air up to the heights of the sky, overturning them, making burning stones follow them, and submerging them in water suited to their deed, by its stench and its uselessness. What is stored up for them in the Hereafter is greater.

(p-468)

When He, glorified is He, had placed first the most important of the narratives that indicate His oath and what He swore by, namely the hidden causes within them despite their existence, and then what they contain of the sending down from the heaven of that which carries the threat, with fire and water, which was alluded to by *al-Muqassimat* (the "dividing" [oaths]), along with the separation between the Muslim and the criminal, He followed them with the story of the one whom He strengthened with *Hamilat* (the "burden-carrying" [winds]), in which there is rain, hail, and blazing fire, as its explanation has passed in *al-A'raf*. Then, after that, [He mentioned] the wind that split the sea, dried up its floor, and into which Pharaoh and the Copts entered. The matter is clear that it was a cause of their destruction while they did not perceive it. So He said, conjoining it to what is implied in the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, or to what is apparent in ﴿And on the earth [are signs]﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 20], or to the "fi" (in) found in His saying ﴿And We left therein a sign for those who fear﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 37]. This is closer and more preferable than other options: ﴿And in Moses [is a sign]﴾, meaning: in his story and his affair there is a great sign of that, ﴿when We sent him﴾ with Our majesty, ﴿to Pharaoh﴾, who had wronged Ibrahim, peace be upon him, after their great kindness to him and to all his people, through what Yusuf, peace be upon him, had done for them, ﴿with clear authority﴾, meaning: manifest miracles in themselves, which, because of the intensity of their (p-469) manifestness, proclaimed that they were miracles. Thus there was in them a clear proof of the truth of his threat, and yet their knowledge of them did not benefit them. For this reason He made the consequence of that and followed it with His saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 39:

﴿So he turned away﴾, i.e., he imposed upon himself turning away after its knowledge had called him to turn toward it. He indicated his turning away by His words: ﴿with his power﴾, i.e., by means of what he relied upon of strength in himself and of his helpers and his armies, or with all of his armies, as a metaphor for exaggeration in turning away.

﴿And said﴾, informing of his incapacity regarding what had come to him with it, while he was not aware: ﴿"A magician"﴾. Then he contradicted himself as you contradict, so he said, in his ignorance of what his own words entail: ﴿"Or a madman"﴾, i.e., due to his audacity against me despite the great kingdom I have, with such a one who calls to what he calls to and threatens over it.

And when this consolation was given to the friends (of God) by this, Almighty God said, warning the enemies: ﴿So We seized him﴾, meaning a seizure of wrath and subjugation by Our majesty, through what We had led him on with and weakened him with of the punishment, which includes a cloud carrying water, hail, fire, and thunderbolts, ﴿and his hosts﴾ [meaning] all of them. ﴿So We threw them﴾, meaning We cast them, casting one who despises them, [as one who regards them with contempt] as pebbles are cast, ﴿into the sea﴾, meaning [the sea (al-bahr)] which deserves to be [sought out], after We had sent the wind upon it, and it drowned him when Musa, peace be upon him, struck it with his staff, and the wind dried its ground, so it made dry what was revealed in it of the paths for the salvation of Our friends and the destruction of Our enemies. ﴿And he was﴾, meaning, and the state was that Fir'awn was ﴿blameworthy (mulim)﴾, meaning one who has come with what fully deserves blame. It is also permissible (p-470) that it be a circumstantial clause (hal) from ﴿the sea (al-yamm)﴾, in the sense that he did to them the act of one who blames, from alamahu, when he exaggerates in rebuking him and becomes one who blames (la'imah), i.e., for them; from alama, intransitive. And it is permissible that it be a contraction from la'ama (with hamza), so the meaning is: ﴿he is one who reforms (muslih)﴾, i.e., he performs the act of those who reform, in saving the friends and drowning the enemies by joining together and closing over them. In al-Qamus (it is said): al-lawm is blame; lama yalumu lawman, alamahu and lawwamahu for emphasis; and alama: he came to what one is blamed for, or became one who blames; and la'amahu with hamza, like mana'ahu, attributed him to blame; and al-sahm: he repaired it, like alamahu and la'amahu, so it was mended. It does not harm Yunus, peace be upon him, that an expression of this kind be used concerning him, for the causes of blame differ just as the causes of disobedience differ, in His saying: ﴿And they disobeyed His messengers﴾ [Hud: 59] and ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord﴾ [Taha: 121]. According to this, the difference between the self of the one who blames and the self of the one who disobeys also varies.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 41:

When he had completed the account of the one for whom the clouds, the water, the fire and the wind were gathered, he followed it with the account of those upon whom came a wind that scatters (dhāriyah), the like of which had never been found, whose origin had existed among them while they were unaware of it; indeed, it had nearly reached them while they thought it was something that would benefit them. ﴿And in ʿĀd﴾, meaning: a great sign, ﴿when﴾, meaning: at the time when ﴿We sent﴾ by Our might ﴿upon them﴾ a sending of dominance and seizure, ﴿the wind﴾, so it came to them carrying a black cloud, scattering the sand and pelting with stones in a manner that could not be endured, ﴿barren﴾, meaning: that which has no fruit, so it does not fertilize trees, nor does it produce clouds, nor does it bring rain, nor mercy (p-471) nor blessing in it. Therefore it destroyed them with a destruction that left no trace. Then he explained its barrenness and its causing of barrenness by his saying:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 42:

﴿Ma tadhar﴾ means: it leaves [them] in a wretched state. He intensified the negation and said: ﴿min shay'in﴾ (of anything). And since their destruction was only by a Doer who chooses (al-fa'il al-mukhtar), he drew attention to this with the particle of elevation (adat al-isti'la'), saying: ﴿Atat 'alayhi﴾ (it came upon it), i.e., coming in accordance with the will of the One who sent it. It overpowered it, both outwardly and inwardly. As for those whose mercy was intended, such as Hud (peace be upon him) and those with him (radiya Allahu 'anhum), they were a spirit and a relief for them, not upon them. ﴿Illa ja'alathu ka'l-rameem﴾ (except that it made it like the rameem), i.e., the thing that has decayed, which the days and nights have worn away, so that decay reduced it to the state of ash. In their speech, it is what has dried up of the plants of the earth and been crushed. This is the statement of Ibn Jurayj. By the expression "tadhar" (it leaves), Hud (peace be upon him) and the believers with him (radiya Allahu 'anhum ajma'in) were excluded, for it left them in a good state, and no evil touched them from it, as was indicated by the particle of elevation regarding the like of this.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 43:

When he had completed what the context of the surah required concerning the account of the people of the Wind that scatters (al-Rih al-Dhariyah), he followed it with the account of those who were destroyed by what the clouds carry of wind and by what the wind carries of the sound of the resounding, crushing Cry (al-Sayhah al-Rajifah al-Mahiqah). So he said: ﴿And in Thamud﴾, that is, the people of Salih, peace be upon him, there is a great sign likewise ﴿when it was said to them﴾, that is, when it was said to them by the One who does not break His promise: ﴿Enjoy yourselves﴾, that is, with the milk of the she-camel and other things with which We have established you, such as crops and palm trees, dwellings in the mountains and plains, and other great blessings which We have commanded you to have, ﴿and do not transgress﴾; ﴿for a time appointed﴾, that is, a term We have set for your lifetimes.

ﷺ-free passage, so no honorifics needed except none present. Note "عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ" appears: render as "peace be upon him".

**﴿So they acted arrogantly﴾**, that is, they committed, because of Our favour to them, *al-'utuw* (arrogance and refusal), which is haughtiness and defiance, **﴿against the command of their Lord﴾**, that is, their Master, whose greatest favour to them was [His bounty]; so they hamstrung the she-camel (p-472) and intended to kill His Prophet, peace be upon him. **﴿Then the thunderbolt seized them﴾** because of their arrogance, as a seizing of subjugation and punishment, **﴿the thunderbolt﴾**, that is, the great cry that the wind carried, bringing it to their ears with the utmost force, and it shook their dwellings with a shaking that removed their souls through the stunning. His words **﴿while they were looking on﴾** indicate that it came from a cloud, and that there was fire in it. It is also permissible, while it is from *al-nazar* (looking), that it be from *al-intizar* (awaiting) as well; for they had been promised the descent of the punishment after three days, and for each day a sign was set for them which befell them, so they were certain of its occurrence on the fourth day.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 45:

﴿Fa-mā﴾, that is: as a consequence of that, ﴿they were not able﴾, that is: they had no power, and he emphasized the negation, saying: ﴿to stand up﴾, that is: after its coming, since it hastened upon them and destroyed them so that they could not stand up.

Since a person may be unable to stand up because of an impediment in his legs, and may defend himself against his enemy by the reasoning of his mind and the planning of his opinion, he said: ﴿Nor were they ones who could defend themselves﴾, that is: in no way whatsoever were they capable of being victorious, neither by themselves nor with a helper who would aid them so that they might obey him in the aid, because their readiness for that had fallen away in every respect.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 51, verse 46:

When he had completed the account of those who were destroyed by that which is characteristically destructive, namely the thunderbolt (al-ṣā'iqa), he followed it with the account of those who were destroyed by that which is characteristically life-giving, namely water, most of which is contained in the rain-clouds (al-ḥalamāt) that the scattering winds (al-Dhāriyāt) stirred up. They were present on the earth and in the sky, and the means of their salvation were prepared, yet they were unaware of any of that. As for Our believing servants, We prepared for them the means of deliverance, such as the ship and other things, and informed them of it. So everything We willed came to pass, and Our friends (awliyā'unā) spoke of it on Our behalf. He then altered the style to draw attention to the greatness of the destruction itself, since it was by that which is characteristically life-giving, preservation, and control over the means: ﴿وقوم﴾ (And the people), i.e., and We destroyed the people of ﴿نوح﴾ (Nuh), given their large numbers, their strength in striving, and their capacity to carry out what they intended. It is also permissible that it be in the accusative as a coordinate of "fīhā" (in it), i.e., "and We left them as a sign." This grammatical analysis (i'rāb) is strengthened by the fact that they all perished, they were all the people of the earth, and their punishment encompassed the whole earth, so they became the sign. This grammatical analysis is supported by the recitation (qirā'a) of Abū 'Amr, Ḥamza, and al-Kisā'ī, who read it in the genitive as a coordinate of the pronoun in "fīhā" (in it).

Since their destruction, despite its magnitude and wide reach, belonged to a period of time, he introduced the preposition, saying ﴿من قبل﴾ (from before), i.e., before all these nations. Then he gave the reason for their destruction in his words ﴿إنهم كانوا﴾ (indeed they were) by nature and disposition, with no means for anyone else among the people of the means to set them right, ﴿قوما﴾ (a people), i.e., powerful, ﴿فاسقين﴾ (defiant), i.e., deeply immersed in going outside the enclosure of religion.

(p. 473)

When the destruction of them was by the water that descended from the sky and emerged from the earth without measure, it might have been thought by someone that this was due to a defect in the two (the sky and the earth), which was then set right afterwards, as happens to some kings who make a construction and strive to perfect it, and it then becomes defective. He said, coordinating with what was made to govern "the day" (yawm), clarifying that the doing of that was not by choice, and indicating His oneness through the completeness of the [power] which indicates what preceded concerning the matter of resurrection: ﴿And the sky We built﴾ with what We have of greatness, ﴿with power (bi-aydin)﴾, i.e., with strength and tremendous might, whose measure cannot be estimated. And since the sky was most fitting, by its greatness and purity, for the attributes of divinity, He said, emphasizing against what their denial of resurrection necessarily entails of disparagement of power: ﴿And indeed, We are expanding it﴾ (lamuwsi'un), despite Our greatness in that, i.e., We are rich and capable, possessors of an endless expanse, that is, of power, from al-wus' (spaciousness), which is subtlety. Likewise, We have expanded the extent of its mass and what is in it of provision for its inhabitants. So the earth in its entirety, despite its vastness, is like a point in the middle of the circle of the sky, by what the attribute of divinity requires, in which partnership is not valid at all. And We are able (mutiqun) for what cannot be counted of the like of that, and of what is greater than it, which is endless, and We encompass everything in power and knowledge, and We are worthy and entitled that this be among Our attributes, so that We are described by it, due to the power over everything We will that is witnessed in Us. We are not like those kings known to you, for when they act they cannot do anything greater than it, and even if they are able, that is with difficulty and hardship. And you will see on the Last Day what vanishes and what you seek in comparison to it. And from Our expansiveness is Our making it without pillars, along with its greatness, and other matters that break customary norms:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 48:

﴿And the earth – We have spread it out﴾ – thus, by Our majesty, it became smoothed and fit for things to settle upon it, and this is a sign of Our smoothing of the earth of Paradise, Our splitting of its rivers, and Our planting of its trees. ﴿How excellent﴾ – that is: it follows from this that it is said in praise of Us: how excellent are ﴿the Spreaders﴾ – that is, We, for the perfection of Our power. Nothing descends from (p-475) the heaven and nothing springs from the earth except by Our will, Our decree, and Our choice from eternity, for when We make something We know what will come from it from the time of its creation until the time of its growth, and nothing from it occurs except by Our decree. This is a reminder of Paradise and Hell: whatever is above them of good is a sign of Paradise, and whatever is in them of mountains, valleys, rough terrain and thorny ground is a sign of Hell.

When the opposites found in a single thing indicate His power more clearly in this respect, He said: ﴿And of everything﴾, that is, of animals and other things, ﴿We created﴾ by Our greatness. Since the philosophers (*al-Falasifa*) say that only one thing arises from one, He said, refuting them: ﴿pairs﴾, that is, two things like it, each of which alternates with the other in one respect, even though it differs from it in another. The benefit of neither is complete without the other, among animals, plants, and other things. This includes opposites: wealth and poverty, beauty and ugliness, life and death, light and darkness, night and day, health and sickness, land and sea, plain and mountain, sun and moon, heat and cold, and the heavens and the earth. That heat and cold come from the very nature of Hell is a clear sign of it, and their being balanced in certain states is a sign of Paradise, reminding of it and stirring longing for it.

Since this is the greatest indication that each of the two pair needs the other, and that the matter must end at one who has no like, and that after this reminder no great reflection is needed, He said: ﴿so that you may remember﴾. He assimilated the *tā'* of the *tafa''ul* form, which indicates effort, striving, and action, so that it became *fatakūnū*, and the sense became: you would be in the position of one who considers that matter with true consideration, hoping that you would remember a little of what is to be remembered, so that He would guide you to the right path. (p-476)

When everything other than Him necessarily has an opposite that opposes it or an counterpart that fills its place, while Glorified is He has no like, because if He had a like, that like would contend with Him, and He would not be able to do everything He wills. ﴿Had there been in them gods other than Allah, they would both have been ruined﴾ [al-Anbiya: 22]. It is established that He destroyed the earlier generations for opposing the Messengers, upon them be blessings and peace. Thus it is established that behind the accountable there is a punishment from which they are right to flee. It is also established that everything other than Him is in need of its pair, which proves that all things are in need of Him, and that no created thing is sufficient in everything that is sought from it. Therefore one must seek refuge only in the One, the Self-Sufficient. Hence He then said, causally connected to this: ﴿So flee﴾, that is, turn towards Him and take refuge in Him. Since He had trained His servants in this surah extensively through the attribute of Lordship, so that they became qualified to penetrate the unseen, and since worship is not sincere except when it is attached to the Essence (al-dhat) and not to anything else, He mentioned the name of the Essence, saying: ﴿to Allah﴾, that is, to the One who has no equal to match Him, to whom all perfection belongs, who is in the utmost exaltedness, so that no one finds rest or tranquillity in a needy being like himself; for the needy has no independence in its own right, and Glorified is He, not at rest with such a being.

Except for one who strips himself from the lowest depths of his bodily hindrances to the zenith of his spiritual attributes. This runs from His threat to His promise, which are indicated by the two pairs (zawjayn). The context therefore moves through warning, entreaty and invitation. It belongs to the category of: "There is no refuge from You except in You; I seek refuge in You from You." It continues to the end of (p. 477) the surah in mentioning Him, as an indication of the sublimity of His command. Then he gave the reason, by saying, emphasising what they have of denial: ﴿Indeed I am to you from Him﴾, that is, not from anyone else, ﴿a warner﴾, that is, against anyone fleeing to other than Him, for he will not attain his aim.

When he had established the rational proof, so evident that anyone can know it within himself, for what he said in this unique statement, he said: ﴿clear﴾. So the flight of the common people is from ignorance to knowledge, in belief and in striving; from laziness to diligence, out of caution and resolve; from constriction to expansiveness, in trust and hope. The flight of the elite is from good to witnessing (shuhud, direct contemplation of Truth), from outward forms (rusum) to foundations (usul), and from personal portions (huzuz) to detachment (tajrid, stripping away of self-interest). The flight of the elite of the elite is from what is other than the Truth to the Truth, in bearing witness in the witnessing of His majesty and in being absorbed in His oneness. Al-Qushayri said: "Whoever's flight to Allah is sound, his flight with Allah is sound." End of quotation. This is with complete adherence to the path, and whoever understands from it any unity (ittihad) with an attribute or an essence has lost the limit of the path of these people, and upon him is the curse of Allah.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 51:

When it was established that there is no refuge except in Allah, the One, exalted above having a partner, and that is Allah, to whom belongs all perfection, and it might have occurred to someone's mind that there exists in existence, apart from the two known pairs, someone we could resort to, just as we resort to a king's vizier, his chamberlain, and the like of what leads to him, He said, warning against His assaults: ﴿And do not set up﴾, that is, by your own desires, ﴿with Allah﴾ — and He repeated the Greatest Name and did not use a pronoun, to specify the intended meaning, because no one shares with Him in this name, and to draw attention to what He has of the attributes of perfection, and to generalize the aspects of the intended meanings, lest it be supposed. It was also said: "with Him" means that the intended prohibition is against setting up [a partner] from the standpoint of flight, not from any other standpoint ﴿another god﴾.

Since the intended meaning is complete clarity of exposition, [He] prevented the metaphor of abstraction, preventing the obstinacy of one who attacks by multiplying the names, as He indicated by His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Isra: 110], and so on. By His saying: ﴿another﴾. Then He gave the reason for the prohibition, with emphasis, because of their attacks on his warning, so He said: ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him﴾, that is: not from anyone else, for anyone else cannot prevent anything, ﴿a warner﴾, that is: one who warns of everlasting destruction through the punishment from which there is no escape if you do that, ﴿clear﴾, that is: I do not say anything from clear transmission except that its evidence is manifest from plain reason.

When He had mentioned their divergent speech, from which is the denial of the Messenger (ﷺ) and attributing to him sorcery, madness and other such arts, and from it is associating partners with Allah, although they acknowledge that there is no creator except Allah and no remover of harm except Him, along with other kinds of confusion, and He informed of their destruction upon that and warned them of it and pointed to it, until He concluded with warning against whoever takes another god, He said, consoling:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 52:

﴿Thus﴾, i.e., like the saying of your people, which is greatly disparate and monstrous in its ugliness, far from the truth, with all its confusion, befell those before them. He indicated this implied element by His words, in a resumptive manner: ﴿Never came to those before them﴾. Since the messengers were sent only in some of the past eras and did not encompass all of them in actuality, He affirmed the preposition in His words ﴿before them﴾ and generalized the negation with His words ﴿any messenger﴾, i.e., from Allah, ﴿but they said﴾, even if some of them said it with the approval of the rest: ﴿"A sorcerer or a madman."﴾ This is because the messenger comes to them contrary to what they are accustomed to, those customs to which their desires had led them. And it is desire that necessitated for them this apparent contradiction, whether the particle "aw" (or) is for distribution, in that some of them said one thing and others said another, or it is for doubt; because the sorcerer is intelligent and clever, bringing what many people are unable to bring, while the madman is the opposite of that. Then He marvelled at them with His words:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 53:

﴿Have they bequeathed this to one another?﴾ [That is:] some of the earlier and later generations enjoined this upon one another.

When he (al-Biqa'i) presented this in the form of a question, as an indication of a saying whose cause one should ask about because of its obscurity, he answered it by saying that they did not enjoin it upon one another, because the earlier generations did not assemble with the later generations. ﴿Rather, they are﴾ united in a quality that led them to that: that they are ﴿a people﴾, that is, possessed of arrogance and pride, ﴿who transgress﴾, that is, who exceed bounds in disbelief, who go to excess in wrongdoing and sins, and who overstep the measure. By using the pronoun he indicated that transgression is an inherent matter for them. Hence He, glory be to Him, is praised for being the One who subdued them by driving them to their destruction, by His perfect power and His all-encompassing knowledge.

And when the Prophet ﷺ was almost destroying his noble self—may my father and mother be sacrificed for him—out of grief over them and sorrow at their turning away from Islam, and fear that he had not fulfilled what was incumbent upon him of warning and notification, Allah, exalted is He, made the following statement a consequence of their condition: (p-480) ﴿So turn away from them﴾, meaning: burden yourself with turning away from striving to convey to them through argument and open harshness, after what has already proceeded from you of conveying [the message]. ﴿So you are not﴾, by reason of turning away after warning, ﴿blameworthy﴾, meaning: deserving of blame because of the turning away of those among them who turned away from you. For I have only decreed this because I have only divided people into a believer, whom the reminder benefits, and a transgressor, whom nothing benefits. Therefore He said:

"And remind," that is, with gentleness and softness. When they persisted in denial and aversion, to the point that he despaired of them, he emphasized what the reminder had caused, with His saying: ﴿Indeed, the reminder﴾, that is, the remembrance through the eloquent warning, ﴿benefits the believers﴾, that is, those whom God has decreed to be firmly rooted in the attribute of faith. Reminding must be repeated much, so that what they hold of impulses of worldly portions and diversions of desires may be overcome, along with what they are naturally disposed to, namely forgetfulness.

When this might give the impression that others are not subject to His power over them, He said, emphasizing it with restriction (*al-ḥaṣr*), indicating that He is the One who divided people into tyrants and believers. It is connected by conjunction (*al-ʿaṭf*) to what is implied: "No one other than Me decreed for them that misguidance and guidance, and I did not send the messengers or reveal the books except to separate out the believers and establish proof against the astray: ﴿And I did not create the jinn and humankind﴾ (most of whom are disbelievers) ﴿except that they worship Me﴾, i.e., that they be brought under My decrees in a manner by which they benefit or harm themselves, not for anything that reaches Me of benefit or harm from it. For I (p. 481) have made them weak and placed in them the impulses of desire, and I have composed in them natural dispositions, and I have prepared them to follow guidance. So whoever obeys his intellect is one who worships Me, fleeing to Me while still running under the will, in a legal (*sharʿiyyah*) and commanded (*amriyyah*) worship by which he gains reward. Whoever obeys desire is one who worships Me while opposing My command, in a volitional (*irādiyyah*) and compelled (*qasriyyah*) worship by which he deserves punishment. Every follower of his desire, if he investigates thoroughly, knows that the good lies in other than what he is committing, and his being bound to what he is in, while knowing that other than it is better for him, is nothing but the compulsion of My will. So this is a linguistic ('*ubūdiyyah lughawiyyah*) worship, and that is a legal worship. What was said at the end of Hud is useful here. All of this is the meaning of Ibn ʿAbbas's statement: ''except that they acknowledge Me in worship, willingly or unwillingly.''"

When He, glory be to Him, had confined their creation to the purpose of worship, He stated this implication explicitly with His words: ﴿I do not desire from them﴾, that is, at any time whatsoever, and He made the negation general with His words: ﴿any provision﴾, that is, any thing of all things, in a manner that would benefit Me by bringing in or repelling [harm], because I am exalted above receiving benefit or harm, as other masters do with their slaves, seeking to multiply their yields and to be aided by their strength. For I am the Absolutely Rich, and everything is in need of Me. ﴿Nor do I desire﴾ at all ﴿that they feed Me﴾, that is, [that] they provide Me with a particular provision which is food. Herein is an allusion (p-482) to their idols: for they used to do with them what benefits them, and bring them food to eat, yet dogs would often eat it and then urinate upon the idols. Nevertheless, this does not deter them. This verse is evidence that provision is more general than food. The expression "desire" indicates what I have said, that worship is intended, namely, proceeding under the will, sometimes in conformity with the Sharia and sometimes in opposition to it.

Since concern with the matter of provision—though He, glorified is He, has guaranteed it—was preoccupying people away from much of worship, and since a person would suppose that what reached him of provision was due to his own effort, He said, restricting that (idea), emphasizing it to remove those suppositions, giving the reason, turning the speech toward the context of the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam) which none other bears, explicitly stating the intended meaning and reaching, in guidance, the furthest of what is intended: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, i.e., the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, exalted above any taint of deficiency, ﴿He﴾, i.e., not other than Him, ﴿is the Provider (al-Razzaq)﴾, i.e., repeatedly, for every living being and at every time. Then He described Him with what shows the insignificance of that (effort), so He said: ﴿Possessor of strength (dhu al-quwwah)﴾, i.e., whose strength never ceases in any way, ﴿the Firm (al-Matin)﴾, i.e., the Mighty, whose might is perpetual and unending.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 51, verse 59:

When Allah, glorified is He, swore to the truth of His threat against them, and indicated by that, until it encompassed all the aspects of their states, that it was according to His will, and concluded with His power, which has no limit, He made the striking of those who threatened Him a consequence of that. He said, emphasizing it because of their denial: ﴿Indeed, for those who wronged﴾, i.e., those who put things in other than their proper places. And since the oath concerned what they were promised, in that it carries rain, He expressed their portion of it which He had decreed for them with His saying: ﴿a portion﴾, i.e., a share of punishment of long evil, as if, because of its length, it had a tail, and it is upon their sins ﴿like the portion of their companions﴾, i.e., those whose wrongdoing preceded them by denying the messengers. It is, in its resemblance to it, like the bucket that is drawn alongside another bucket, and that is a clear proof that what they are promised is true and that the Religion is certain to occur. ﴿So let them not seek to hasten Me﴾, i.e., let them not ask that I bring it to them before its appointed time that is due for it; for that is not done except by one who is deficient, whereas I am exalted above that. I do not fear missing anything, nor does incapacity reach Me, nor am I described by it, and I will surely bring it upon them at the time I decreed in eternity, for it is the most fitting of times for their punishment, since their sins have become complete. Then it will be—how dreadful is this threat, and how great and how painful is this warning—a matter that no repeller can repel and no preventer can prevent from occurring. For this reason He made His following saying a consequence of it:

Woe, then, to those who disbelieve, (﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾) meaning: the worst condition and punishment, one that calls for lamentation and wailing, (﴿لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾) meaning: those who concealed what was manifest of these proofs, which no sensible person can afford to deny. (﴿مِن يَوْمِهِمُ﴾) He attributed it to them because it is specific to them, and not to the believers, (﴿الَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ﴾) in this world and in the Hereafter. Its last part has corresponded to its first through the truth of the threat, and the emphatic oath has been established for you by conclusive evidence. And God knows best what is correct, and to Him is the return and the final resort.
